title: Normative Reasoning in Large Language Models: A Comparative Benchmark from Logical and Modal Perspectives

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model performance on logical reasoning tasks using premises and conclusions categorized into three content types: congruent (aligns with common sense), incongruent (contradicts common sense), and nonsense. This measures whether the model's logical validity judgments are improperly influenced by the believability of the content.

Comparing the performance of models on structurally similar logical reasoning tasks across two distinct domains: normative (deontic) reasoning and epistemic reasoning, to evaluate if reasoning capabilities are improperly skewed or domain-dependent.
